# M6 handoff prompt

The first chat ran M0 to M5 and filled its context. Paste the text block below as the first message of a new VS Code agent chat on Claude Opus 5.5. The orchestrator of the first chat wrote it after M4 and updates the "State at handoff" section when M5 ends.

```text
You are the orchestrator for milestone M6 of an interview submission in /home/davidt/project/sonrisa-home-task. A previous chat ran M0 to M5 and ran out of context. This prompt carries what that chat learned. Read the files it names before you act, and check every fact here against the repository, because the repository wins when they disagree.

## The task

A product manager's brief: users set up alerts for important world events, such as breaking news, market moves and natural disasters, and get them by email and Slack. More channels must be easy to add, and there is an admin view. The brief is docs/task-04-feature-design-and-build.docx. It is git-ignored, and unzip is not installed, so read it with python3 and zipfile.

The graders evaluate the process, not the product: how the AI was directed, which decisions were made and why, and what output was checked, rejected or corrected. The submission is a GitHub repository with commits for each major milestone, every prompt, the process artifacts, and the deliverables.

## Read first, in this order

1. AGENTS.md
2. docs/plan.md, including the "Milestone commits" table
3. docs/requirements.md and docs/design.md
4. docs/decision-log.md
5. docs/ai-review-log.md
6. docs/prompting-opus-5-5.md
7. prompts/prompt-log.md and the newest files in prompts/subagents/
8. git log --oneline m4..HEAD, for M5

## M6 scope

docs/plan.md says: README, screenshots, final AI review log, chat export. Done when the submission is ready to push. In detail:

1. README.md, which today holds one line. It must cover:
   - what the app does
   - the stack and the AI tooling: VS Code agent mode, an orchestrator on Claude Opus 5.5, implementer subagents, reviewer-opus on Claude Opus 5.5 and reviewer-gpt on GPT-6.2 Sol
   - prerequisites: Node 26, Docker with Compose, and the user in the docker group
   - setup, run and test commands
   - the seeded users
   - a demo script: sign in, add an email target and a Slack target on the mock URL, create an alert, inject an event through the dev route, see the message in the Slack mock and in Mailpit, see the delivery as an admin, turn on the mock's fail mode to show retries, retry a failed delivery
   - where to find the process: plan, requirements, design, decision log, AI review log, reviews, prompts, chat exports, and the milestone tags
   - known limits and the day-two list
2. Screenshots in docs/screenshots/, embedded in the README: sign-in, alerts list, alert form, targets, admin deliveries with several statuses, metrics.
3. A closing entry in docs/ai-review-log.md: patterns across all milestones, such as what each reviewer model found and missed, how the implementers failed, and what the orchestrator caught. Add a list of items that are still open.
4. A final review of the whole repository by both reviewers, reconciled like the others.
5. Tag m6 on the last M6 commit, add it to the table in docs/plan.md, and ask the user to export this chat to prompts/exports/.

Before you change anything, reply with a short M6 plan and your questions, and wait for the user's answer.

## How to work

These rules come from M0 to M5. The evidence is in the AI review log.

- Roles are in AGENTS.md. Implementers are the default subagent: call the subagent tool without an agent name. Reviewers are reviewer-opus and reviewer-gpt; send both the same prompt in parallel.
- Save every subagent prompt to prompts/subagents/NNN-<slug>.md before you send it. Continue from the highest number in that folder.
- Check every subagent prompt against docs/prompting-opus-5-5.md. An implementer prompt names the files to read, lists the tasks and the verification commands, and ends with the implementer block from the last section of that file.
- Give an implementer one area per prompt. Long implementer prompts returned an empty message or a progress note instead of a report (V-011, V-017, V-019).
- After every implementer run, check the work yourself: git status, the diff, and npx nx run-many -t build lint test --skip-nx-cache. Do not rely on the report. Implementers made changes they did not report (D-030, D-035).
- Reviewers share one terminal and the test database. Tell them not to start servers and not to run API specs that use the database. They may run web tests and pure unit specs.
- Before you accept a major finding, read the code or rerun the evidence. Reviewers have been wrong (V-018, V-020 finding F8).
- Save reviewer replies word for word in docs/reviews/<milestone>-<model>.md, under a title and a line that names the prompt. Do not paraphrase (V-015).
- Record every finding as accepted, rejected or deferred, with a reason, in a table in a new docs/ai-review-log.md entry. Continue the V- and D- numbering from the last entry.
- Log every user prompt word for word in prompts/prompt-log.md, numbering on from the last entry. Answers in question forms count. Log this handoff prompt as the first M6 entry by reference to this file.
- Apply .agents/skills/unslop/SKILL.md to everything you write in docs/, prompts/ and README.md. User prompts and reviewer replies stay word for word.
- Commits follow the Angular convention in AGENTS.md. Leave the scope empty when a commit spans projects. Commit after each verified part. Push only when the user asks in the current prompt. Never force-push and never rewrite history (D-036).
- The user's editor runs Prettier on save. Expect diffs that are only formatting. Check them with git diff -w and commit them on their own.
- Run one terminal command at a time. Run set +H before a command that contains "!", or bash history expansion rewrites it.

## Environment facts

- Linux under WSL, Node 26.13.1, npm 11.20, Docker 29 with Compose v5.
- Postgres 18 at 127.0.0.1:5432 with user and password alerts and databases alerts and alerts_test. Mailpit v1.34.0 with SMTP on 127.0.0.1:1025 and the web UI and REST API on 127.0.0.1:8025.
- The agent shell started before the user joined the docker group, and sg and newgrp are not installed, so docker commands fail with "permission denied". Ask the user to run them. Postgres and Mailpit still work over TCP.
- npm uses a company Artifactory registry that lacks some packages, such as @ng-icons (D-034). Run npm view before you plan on a package.
- .env holds a real JWT secret. Never print it.
- Commands: npm run setup; npm run dev, or npx nx serve api and npx nx serve web started in the background with setsid; npx nx run-many -t build lint test --skip-nx-cache; npm run e2e. Stop the servers you start, including the esbuild and @angular/build processes.
- Seeded users: admin@example.local with admin-password-123, and user@example.local with user-password-123.
- Dev routes: POST /api/dev/events injects an event. The mock Slack receiver takes webhooks at http://localhost:3000/api/dev/mock-slack/<hookId>. GET and DELETE /api/dev/mock-slack/messages read and clear it. PUT /api/dev/mock-slack/mode with {"fail": true} makes it answer 500.
- The VS Code browser keeps its page hidden. Playwright click and Enter wait for a stable frame that never comes. Use page.fill, and page.evaluate with form.requestSubmit() or element.click().
- The VS Code browser runs on the user's machine through port forwarding, so page.screenshot({ path }) does not write into this workspace. The screenshot tool shows you the page but saves nothing. For README screenshots, use the repository's Playwright from the shell if its browser is installed, or ask the user to save them.

## State at handoff

- M0 to M4 are committed and tagged m0 to m4. docs/plan.md maps each tag to its commits.
- M5 adds API integration tests and one Playwright smoke test. Read git log m4..HEAD and the AI review log entries after V-020 for its outcome.
- Open items:
  - V-016: no test has compared Claude Opus 5.5 at medium effort with xhigh. Close it with a reason or leave it open in the closing entry.
  - Lint warnings: an unused _enabled in libs/shared/src/lib/alerts.spec.ts, and the web bundle budget.
  - Deferred review findings in V-014, V-018 and V-020.
  - Known limits in docs/design.md and day-two candidates in docs/plan.md.
- Chat exports: prompts/exports/M1-chat.json and M2-M3-chat.json. The first chat's export for M4 and M5 should be there too. If it is missing, ask the user for it.
```

I added the integration test and it passes. All four scenarios work against the real database, Mailpit and the mock Slack receiver. I committed nothing.

1. **Files added:** `apps/api/src/pipeline.integration.spec.ts` (4 tests). No other files changed.

2. **Command results:**
   - `npx nx test api --skip-nx-cache`: 19 files and 171 tests passed, 4 of them in the new file.
   - `npx nx run-many -t build lint test --skip-nx-cache`: succeeded for all 14 projects. ESLint and `tsc` on the new file are also clean.
   - Two runs in a row of `npx vitest run --config apps/api/vitest.config.mts apps/api/src/pipeline.integration.spec.ts`: 4 of 4 passed both times. Afterwards the test database had 0 users, 0 deliveries and 0 `dev` events, and both channels were on.
   - Rule break (every new delivery `pending` in `apps/api/src/events/ingest.ts`): scenario 4 failed, expected `skipped`, got `pending`. The other 3 passed. I restored the line; `git diff apps/` is empty and the database was clean after the failed run.

3. **API bugs found:** none.

4. **Deviations:**
   - `loadConfig` rejects `DELIVERY_BACKOFF_BASE_MS=0` because the value must be a positive integer. I passed the other overrides through `loadConfig`, then set the backoff to 0 on the parsed result. This doesn't match design.md, whose Tests table calls for "base backoff 0", which the config does not accept.
   - I created the admin user in the database with a hashed password, then logged in through `POST /api/auth/login`. That way the admin cookie also comes over HTTP, like the user's.
   - Cleanup of users, events and fail mode runs after each test, not once at the end. Otherwise an alert from an earlier test would also match later events and change their `deliveriesCreated` count.
   - Scenario 3 also checks `attempts 2` after the second tick, and that the mock received 4 posts: 3 failures and the successful retry.

5. **Not verified:** Mailpit messages from the test runs stay in Mailpit. Each address is random, so later runs don't see them.

I finished all three tasks. `npm run e2e` passed twice in a row, the full build/lint/test passed, and ports 3000 and 4200 are free.

**1. Files**
- [apps/web-e2e/playwright.config.mts](apps/web-e2e/playwright.config.mts): starts the API and web servers as asked and removes the `web:serve-static` CI branch. Chromium only, 1 worker, 0 retries, trace on failure.
- [apps/web-e2e/project.json](apps/web-e2e/project.json): turns off the cache for `e2e` and adds `api` to `implicitDependencies`.
- [apps/web-e2e/src/smoke.spec.ts](apps/web-e2e/src/smoke.spec.ts) added; `src/example.spec.ts` deleted.

**2. Command results**
- `npm run e2e` run 1: passed, test 8.1s, Nx 15.4s.
- `npm run e2e` run 2: passed, test 5.5s, Nx 11.0s. The cleanup deleted the alert and target both times (204).
- `npx playwright test` run directly, so Playwright starts both servers itself: passed, 19.7s.
- `npx nx run-many -t build lint test --skip-nx-cache`: passed, 20 tasks in 14 projects. eslint on web-e2e shows no warnings.
- Leftover processes: none, and ports 3000 and 4200 are free.
- `git status --short`: `M` playwright.config.mts, `M` project.json, `D` src/example.spec.ts, `??` src/smoke.spec.ts. The `prompts/` changes there are not mine.

**3. Locators**
- Deliveries rows have no aria-label. I find the row with `getByRole('row', { name: eventTitle })` and check its `getByText('Sent', { exact: true })`.
- The target checkbox's name includes "(Slack)", so I use `getByRole('checkbox', { name: targetName })`, which matches part of the name.
- The severity options have no plain value attribute, so I select them with `selectOption({ label: '1' })`.

**4. Deviations**
- I removed `getReadyUrl`. When only one server reports its address, Nx passes that one on, and it can be the API's port 3000.
- I added `gracefulShutdown` with SIGTERM. Without it, the direct run left the API running on port 3000 after Playwright exited. I stopped that process myself, since my own run started it.
- I turned off the e2e cache. Otherwise the second run just reads the cached result and runs no test.
- I set the test timeout to 60s, because the two 20s polls plus the UI steps can go past the 30s default.
- The prompt didn't set the event severity or symbol, so I used severity 1 and symbol `E2E`.
- The test clicks Refresh on every poll, not only when the row is not sent yet. Doing it only when needed would mean an `if` inside the test, which the Playwright lint rules warn about.

**5. Not verified**
- A CI environment.
- The injected events stay in the database, because the API has no endpoint to delete them.

### Findings

| ID  | Severity | Location | Finding | Evidence | Suggested fix |
| --- | -------- | -------- | ------- | -------- | ------------- |
| F1 | major | apps/web-e2e/src/smoke.spec.ts:105 | `deliveriesCreated: 1` counts every match in the dev database, not only this test's alert. The run fails if the dev database has another enabled market alert with empty symbols, a minimum change of 8 or less and minimum severity 1. That can be a reviewer's demo alert, or an `E2E market <old suffix>` alert left behind when cleanup failed. Cleanup at :51 deletes only the current run's names, so one failed cleanup breaks every run after it. | `matchEvent` in events/ingest.ts selects every enabled alert in the category. seed.ts creates no alerts. | Assert `>= 1`: the hook message and the admin row already prove this alert matched. Or delete every `E2E ` alert and target before the test. |
| F2 | minor | apps/api/src/pipeline.integration.spec.ts:387 | Slack is disabled before the `try`. If the check inside `setChannelEnabled` fails, or the run is killed during scenario 4, Slack stays off in `alerts_test`. Nothing turns it back on: `syncRegistryRows` does nothing on conflict, and worker.spec's afterEach turns only email back on. After that, scenarios 1 and 3 and ingest.spec's "two pending rows" test fail on every run. | registry-sync.ts `onConflictDoNothing`. worker.spec.ts:81 | Move the disable call into the `try`. Enable all channels in `beforeAll`. |
| F3 | minor | pipeline.integration.spec.ts:302, :304 | `worker.tick()` claims the 10 oldest due rows in the whole database. `deliveriesCreated` counts all alerts. The random suffixes therefore do not keep two runs on `alerts_test` apart, as with two reviewers running at once. One run's worker can claim the other run's rows and fail them, because the other run's mock port is not in its allowlist. | worker.ts `claim()` has no scope. `orderBy(asc(nextAttemptAt)).limit(10)` | State the one-run-at-a-time rule in the design, or assert on `deliveriesOf(alertId)` instead of the global count. |
| F4 | minor | docs/design.md:407 | The design is now out of date in three places. It says `npm run e2e` runs "against a running stack", but Nx now starts `api:serve` and `web:serve` itself. It says delivery tests use `listen({ port: 0 })`, but the spec calls `freePort()` and then listens, which leaves a small race. It points to Mailpit's `/messages`, but the spec uses `/search`. | `nx show project web-e2e`: e2e dependsOn `api:serve`, `web:serve`, `waitFor: ready` | Update the Commands and Tests sections. |
| F5 | nit | apps/web-e2e/playwright.config.mts:8 | The comment reads as if Playwright starts the servers. Under `npm run e2e`, Nx starts them, because the plugin turns any webServer with `reuseExistingServer: true` into a dependency. `gracefulShutdown` therefore applies only to a direct `npx playwright test`. Also, `e2e-ci--src/smoke.spec.ts` still has `cache: true`. | @nx/playwright plugin.js:585. `nx show project` output | Say so in the comment. Turn caching off for `e2e-ci` too. |

### Verified

- The pipeline tests fail when the behaviour they name breaks:
  - Scenario 1 checks that both rows are sent, that Mailpit has a `[market]` subject and that the mock Slack message holds the alert name.
  - Scenario 3 checks failed, failed, then dead at attempt 3, and that the retry resets attempts to 0 and clears `lastError`. It also requires exactly 4 mock posts, so an extra send after dead fails the test.
  - Scenario 4 checks `skipped` with `channel disabled`, and the email row `pending`.
  - Scenario 2 alone would pass with a matcher that rejects everything, but scenario 1 catches that.
- In the e2e test, wrong form values change `deliveriesCreated` or block the create. The admin row is found by its unique title, and `Sent` comes from labels.ts. While the page loads, Refresh is disabled, and `click()` waits for it.
- Timing:
  - The pipeline test calls `tick()` by hand.
  - With base 0, `msFromNow(0)` makes the next retry due on the next tick.
  - The e2e test has two 20 s polls against a 2 s worker poll inside a 60 s test timeout.
  - `vi.waitFor` waits 1 s by default. That is low risk, because Mailpit stores a message before it answers DATA.
- Cleanup runs on failure in both files: afterEach deletes the users, which cascades, and the events, and turns fail mode off. afterAll deletes the admin.
- `reuseExistingServer: true` is required, because Nx already holds the ports when Playwright starts. Removing the `serve-static` CI branch fixes M2-04. `gracefulShutdown` exists in the types of Playwright 1.65.1. The fixed `retries: 0` overrides the preset's CI value.
- Every item in the design's Integration row has a spec: auth, alerts, admin, ingest (including the duplicate rerun and skipped rows), worker (including lease expiry and stale results) and the pipeline spec. The E2E row and N5 are covered. Still untested: an email failure through real SMTP, and the source switches end to end. Neither is in the contract.
- `nx lint` passes for `api` and `web-e2e`.
- Both commits follow AGENTS.md. Types and scopes are valid, the summaries are imperative and lowercase with no period, the bodies explain why, and each commit touches one project.
- Prompts 024 to 026 and `prompt-log.md` are not committed yet. M4 committed its records in a final docs commit, so this matches.

### Not verified

- I did not run the e2e test, the API specs or the mutation checks, because the prompt does not allow it.
- What `npm run e2e` does while `npm run dev` is already running. Nx would try to start a second `api:serve` on port 3000.
- The `.env` values for the rate limit, `WORKER_POLL_MS` and the Slack allowlist, because I did not print `.env`. Each run logs in 3 times. The default limit is 10 per minute.

The web port file is tracked, so I found no fresh-checkout issue there. I’ll keep the final review focused on the cleanup failures, assertion gaps, and timing risks the source supports, and mark the live checks I didn’t rerun.

### Findings

| ID | Severity | Location | Finding | Evidence | Suggested fix |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| M5-01 | major | [apps/api/src/pipeline.integration.spec.ts:135](apps/api/src/pipeline.integration.spec.ts#L135) | A failed mock reset skips DB cleanup. A failed admin deletion skips app and pool shutdown. The Slack switch is disabled before `try`, so a failed response assertion after the write can leave Slack disabled for later specs. | [Teardown](apps/api/src/pipeline.integration.spec.ts#L148) and [switch setup](apps/api/src/pipeline.integration.spec.ts#L387). | Attempt cleanup steps independently. Capture the original switch value and restore it even if disabling fails. |
| M5-02 | major | [apps/web-e2e/src/smoke.spec.ts:105](apps/web-e2e/src/smoke.spec.ts#L105) | The count is global. Existing alerts can receive the injected event and fail the assertion. If cleanup login or alert deletion fails, the leftover wildcard alert can break the next run too. | [Matcher](apps/api/src/events/ingest.ts#L49) and [cleanup](apps/web-e2e/src/smoke.spec.ts#L51). | Use a disposable seeded DB, a unique market symbol, and cleanup by captured IDs. |
| M5-03 | minor | [apps/web-e2e/src/smoke.spec.ts:108](apps/web-e2e/src/smoke.spec.ts#L108) | A different event sent to the same hook can satisfy the Slack poll. Both specs can pass if notification payloads omit the event title. The UI test also passes if it saves a threshold of zero instead of five, since it only injects an 8% move. | [Hook-only poll](apps/web-e2e/src/smoke.spec.ts#L112) and [pipeline payload checks](apps/api/src/pipeline.integration.spec.ts#L309). | Assert the injected title in both sinks and verify the saved threshold or inject a below-threshold event. |
| M5-04 | minor | [apps/web-e2e/src/smoke.spec.ts:114](apps/web-e2e/src/smoke.spec.ts#L114) | A busy batch can take 20 s before the next 2 s worker interval starts, exceeding the 20 s Slack poll. The admin poll can also spend its budget waiting for Refresh to become enabled. | [Worker scheduling](apps/api/src/delivery/worker.ts#L230), [configured timing](docs/design.md#L385), and [Refresh](apps/web/src/app/admin/deliveries-page.html#L37). | Isolate the queue, budget for the worker deadline plus its interval, and wait for the refresh response. |
| M5-05 | minor | [apps/api/src/pipeline.integration.spec.ts:100](apps/api/src/pipeline.integration.spec.ts#L100) | The port probe releases its socket before Fastify binds, so another process can take it. The Mailpit poll also inherits a 1 s limit inside Vitest’s 5 s test budget. | [Port release](apps/api/src/pipeline.integration.spec.ts#L61), [Mailpit poll](apps/api/src/pipeline.integration.spec.ts#L309), and installed Vitest defaults. | Bind once on port `0` as designed. Set explicit poll, request, and test deadlines. |
| M5-06 | minor | [apps/web-e2e/playwright.config.mts:6](apps/web-e2e/playwright.config.mts#L6) | `BASE_URL` can point browser traffic at a different stack from the fixed readiness and webhook URLs. Reuse also accepts stale code or a stack with Slack disabled. | [Readiness config](apps/web-e2e/playwright.config.mts#L40) and [webhook URL](apps/web-e2e/src/smoke.spec.ts#L28). | Keep the endpoints tied to one stack and make reuse explicit. |

### Verified

- Uncached API and e2e lint passed; `git diff --check` was clean. Both commits comply with `AGENTS.md`.
- The suite covers the design matrix and N5 by inspection, subject to the assertion gaps above. Earlier specs cover dedup, lease expiry, stale results, queued-channel pause/resume, and backoff calculation. M5’s manual ticks do not test elapsed retry delays.
- The proxied web server replaces the static CI branch. Chromium runs with one worker, no retries, and caching off. Playwright requests `SIGTERM` for servers it launches and leaves reused servers alone.

### Not verified

- Live specs, mutations, CI startup, port release, and failure-path cleanup were not rerun under the review constraints.

# M5 review by reviewer-opus (Claude Opus 5.5)

Prompt: `prompts/subagents/026-review-m5.md`. The text below the line is the reviewer's reply, word for word.

---

### Findings

| ID  | Severity | Location | Finding | Evidence | Suggested fix |
| --- | -------- | -------- | ------- | -------- | ------------- |
| F1 | major | apps/web-e2e/src/smoke.spec.ts:105 | `deliveriesCreated: 1` counts every match in the dev database, not only this test's alert. The run fails if the dev database has another enabled market alert with empty symbols, a minimum change of 8 or less and minimum severity 1. That can be a reviewer's demo alert, or an `E2E market <old suffix>` alert left behind when cleanup failed. Cleanup at :51 deletes only the current run's names, so one failed cleanup breaks every run after it. | `matchEvent` in events/ingest.ts selects every enabled alert in the category. seed.ts creates no alerts. | Assert `>= 1`: the hook message and the admin row already prove this alert matched. Or delete every `E2E ` alert and target before the test. |
| F2 | minor | apps/api/src/pipeline.integration.spec.ts:387 | Slack is disabled before the `try`. If the check inside `setChannelEnabled` fails, or the run is killed during scenario 4, Slack stays off in `alerts_test`. Nothing turns it back on: `syncRegistryRows` does nothing on conflict, and worker.spec's afterEach turns only email back on. After that, scenarios 1 and 3 and ingest.spec's "two pending rows" test fail on every run. | registry-sync.ts `onConflictDoNothing`. worker.spec.ts:81 | Move the disable call into the `try`. Enable all channels in `beforeAll`. |
| F3 | minor | pipeline.integration.spec.ts:302, :304 | `worker.tick()` claims the 10 oldest due rows in the whole database. `deliveriesCreated` counts all alerts. The random suffixes therefore do not keep two runs on `alerts_test` apart, as with two reviewers running at once. One run's worker can claim the other run's rows and fail them, because the other run's mock port is not in its allowlist. | worker.ts `claim()` has no scope. `orderBy(asc(nextAttemptAt)).limit(10)` | State the one-run-at-a-time rule in the design, or assert on `deliveriesOf(alertId)` instead of the global count. |
| F4 | minor | docs/design.md:407 | The design is now out of date in three places. It says `npm run e2e` runs "against a running stack", but Nx now starts `api:serve` and `web:serve` itself. It says delivery tests use `listen({ port: 0 })`, but the spec calls `freePort()` and then listens, which leaves a small race. It points to Mailpit's `/messages`, but the spec uses `/search`. | `nx show project web-e2e`: e2e dependsOn `api:serve`, `web:serve`, `waitFor: ready` | Update the Commands and Tests sections. |
| F5 | nit | apps/web-e2e/playwright.config.mts:8 | The comment reads as if Playwright starts the servers. Under `npm run e2e`, Nx starts them, because the plugin turns any webServer with `reuseExistingServer: true` into a dependency. `gracefulShutdown` therefore applies only to a direct `npx playwright test`. Also, `e2e-ci--src/smoke.spec.ts` still has `cache: true`. | @nx/playwright plugin.js:585. `nx show project` output | Say so in the comment. Turn caching off for `e2e-ci` too. |

### Verified

- The pipeline tests fail when the behaviour they name breaks:
  - Scenario 1 checks that both rows are sent, that Mailpit has a `[market]` subject and that the mock Slack message holds the alert name.
  - Scenario 3 checks failed, failed, then dead at attempt 3, and that the retry resets attempts to 0 and clears `lastError`. It also requires exactly 4 mock posts, so an extra send after dead fails the test.
  - Scenario 4 checks `skipped` with `channel disabled`, and the email row `pending`.
  - Scenario 2 alone would pass with a matcher that rejects everything, but scenario 1 catches that.
- In the e2e test, wrong form values change `deliveriesCreated` or block the create. The admin row is found by its unique title, and `Sent` comes from labels.ts. While the page loads, Refresh is disabled, and `click()` waits for it.
- Timing:
  - The pipeline test calls `tick()` by hand.
  - With base 0, `msFromNow(0)` makes the next retry due on the next tick.
  - The e2e test has two 20 s polls against a 2 s worker poll inside a 60 s test timeout.
  - `vi.waitFor` waits 1 s by default. That is low risk, because Mailpit stores a message before it answers DATA.
- Cleanup runs on failure in both files: afterEach deletes the users, which cascades, and the events, and turns fail mode off. afterAll deletes the admin.
- `reuseExistingServer: true` is required, because Nx already holds the ports when Playwright starts. Removing the `serve-static` CI branch fixes M2-04. `gracefulShutdown` exists in the types of Playwright 1.65.1. The fixed `retries: 0` overrides the preset's CI value.
- Every item in the design's Integration row has a spec: auth, alerts, admin, ingest (including the duplicate rerun and skipped rows), worker (including lease expiry and stale results) and the pipeline spec. The E2E row and N5 are covered. Still untested: an email failure through real SMTP, and the source switches end to end. Neither is in the contract.
- `nx lint` passes for `api` and `web-e2e`.
- Both commits follow AGENTS.md. Types and scopes are valid, the summaries are imperative and lowercase with no period, the bodies explain why, and each commit touches one project.
- Prompts 024 to 026 and `prompt-log.md` are not committed yet. M4 committed its records in a final docs commit, so this matches.

### Not verified

- I did not run the e2e test, the API specs or the mutation checks, because the prompt does not allow it.
- What `npm run e2e` does while `npm run dev` is already running. Nx would try to start a second `api:serve` on port 3000.
- The `.env` values for the rate limit, `WORKER_POLL_MS` and the Slack allowlist, because I did not print `.env`. Each run logs in 3 times. The default limit is 10 per minute.

# M5 review by reviewer-gpt (GPT-6.2 Sol)

---

The web port file is tracked, so I found no fresh-checkout issue there. I’ll keep the final review focused on the cleanup failures, assertion gaps, and timing risks the source supports, and mark the live checks I didn’t rerun.

### Findings

| ID | Severity | Location | Finding | Evidence | Suggested fix |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| M5-01 | major | [apps/api/src/pipeline.integration.spec.ts:135](apps/api/src/pipeline.integration.spec.ts#L135) | A failed mock reset skips DB cleanup. A failed admin deletion skips app and pool shutdown. The Slack switch is disabled before `try`, so a failed response assertion after the write can leave Slack disabled for later specs. | [Teardown](apps/api/src/pipeline.integration.spec.ts#L148) and [switch setup](apps/api/src/pipeline.integration.spec.ts#L387). | Attempt cleanup steps independently. Capture the original switch value and restore it even if disabling fails. |
| M5-02 | major | [apps/web-e2e/src/smoke.spec.ts:105](apps/web-e2e/src/smoke.spec.ts#L105) | The count is global. Existing alerts can receive the injected event and fail the assertion. If cleanup login or alert deletion fails, the leftover wildcard alert can break the next run too. | [Matcher](apps/api/src/events/ingest.ts#L49) and [cleanup](apps/web-e2e/src/smoke.spec.ts#L51). | Use a disposable seeded DB, a unique market symbol, and cleanup by captured IDs. |
| M5-03 | minor | [apps/web-e2e/src/smoke.spec.ts:108](apps/web-e2e/src/smoke.spec.ts#L108) | A different event sent to the same hook can satisfy the Slack poll. Both specs can pass if notification payloads omit the event title. The UI test also passes if it saves a threshold of zero instead of five, since it only injects an 8% move. | [Hook-only poll](apps/web-e2e/src/smoke.spec.ts#L112) and [pipeline payload checks](apps/api/src/pipeline.integration.spec.ts#L309). | Assert the injected title in both sinks and verify the saved threshold or inject a below-threshold event. |
| M5-04 | minor | [apps/web-e2e/src/smoke.spec.ts:114](apps/web-e2e/src/smoke.spec.ts#L114) | A busy batch can take 20 s before the next 2 s worker interval starts, exceeding the 20 s Slack poll. The admin poll can also spend its budget waiting for Refresh to become enabled. | [Worker scheduling](apps/api/src/delivery/worker.ts#L230), [configured timing](docs/design.md#L385), and [Refresh](apps/web/src/app/admin/deliveries-page.html#L37). | Isolate the queue, budget for the worker deadline plus its interval, and wait for the refresh response. |
| M5-05 | minor | [apps/api/src/pipeline.integration.spec.ts:100](apps/api/src/pipeline.integration.spec.ts#L100) | The port probe releases its socket before Fastify binds, so another process can take it. The Mailpit poll also inherits a 1 s limit inside Vitest’s 5 s test budget. | [Port release](apps/api/src/pipeline.integration.spec.ts#L61), [Mailpit poll](apps/api/src/pipeline.integration.spec.ts#L309), and installed Vitest defaults. | Bind once on port `0` as designed. Set explicit poll, request, and test deadlines. |
| M5-06 | minor | [apps/web-e2e/playwright.config.mts:6](apps/web-e2e/playwright.config.mts#L6) | `BASE_URL` can point browser traffic at a different stack from the fixed readiness and webhook URLs. Reuse also accepts stale code or a stack with Slack disabled. | [Readiness config](apps/web-e2e/playwright.config.mts#L40) and [webhook URL](apps/web-e2e/src/smoke.spec.ts#L28). | Keep the endpoints tied to one stack and make reuse explicit. |

### Verified

- Uncached API and e2e lint passed; `git diff --check` was clean. Both commits comply with `AGENTS.md`.
- The suite covers the design matrix and N5 by inspection, subject to the assertion gaps above. Earlier specs cover dedup, lease expiry, stale results, queued-channel pause/resume, and backoff calculation. M5’s manual ticks do not test elapsed retry delays.
- The proxied web server replaces the static CI branch. Chromium runs with one worker, no retries, and caching off. Playwright requests `SIGTERM` for servers it launches and leaves reused servers alone.

### Not verified

- Live specs, mutations, CI startup, port release, and failure-path cleanup were not rerun under the review constraints.

```text
You are the implementer for review fixes to the M5 tests in /home/davidt/project/sonrisa-home-task. Do not commit, push or amend. Edit only apps/api/src/pipeline.integration.spec.ts and the files under apps/web-e2e. Do not change application code; if a fix seems to need it, report it instead.

Environment: Postgres and Mailpit run. Chromium for Playwright is installed. Ports 3000 and 4200 are free. No Docker access. Never print .env.

Changes to the e2e test:
1. F1 and M5-02. Other alerts in the dev database can match the injected event, so the count is not this test's to own. Assert deliveriesCreated is at least 1. Give the alert one unique symbol, "E" followed by 7 characters of the suffix in uppercase, and inject the event with that symbol. Before the test, sign in as the user through page.request and delete every alert and target whose name starts with "E2E ", so a run that failed to clean up cannot break the next one.
2. M5-03. The Slack poll waits for a message on the hook whose text contains the injected event title. After the alert is created, read it back through GET /api/alerts and assert its saved filters: the one symbol, direction any, minChangePct 5.

4. F5. Correct the comment in playwright.config.mts: under npm run e2e, Nx starts both servers as dependencies and Playwright reuses them; gracefulShutdown applies only to a direct npx playwright test. Turn caching off for the inferred e2e-ci targets as well.

Changes to the pipeline spec:
5. F2 and M5-01. Enable every channel in beforeAll. In scenario 4, move the disable call inside the try, so the finally block restores the switch even if the disable step fails. 6. M5-05, in part. Give the Mailpit wait an explicit timeout of 5 seconds and the tests that wait on it an explicit timeout of 15 seconds. Keep the free-port probe: the channel registry needs the allowlist prefix, with the port, before the app can listen.
7. M5-03, in part. In scenario 1, also assert that the Mailpit subject and the mock Slack text contain the injected event title.

- npx vitest run --config apps/api/vitest.config.mts apps/api/src/pipeline.integration.spec.ts, twice
- npm run e2e, twice

- npx nx run-many -t build lint test --skip-nx-cache

Your last message goes back to the orchestrator, which cannot reply to you. Finish every task in this prompt before you return. Do not end with a summary that announces the next step, with an offer to do more, or with a list of choices that do not block the work. Stop early only when a task cannot go on without the user. Then name the blocker and list what you finished.

The report, in under 300 words:
1. Files changed.
2. Command results, one line each, including what npm run e2e does while npm run dev runs.
3. Deviations from this prompt, and why.
4. What you could not verify.
```

**What M5 added**
- [pipeline.integration.spec.ts](apps/api/src/pipeline.integration.spec.ts) runs the API on a real port with the real email and Slack channels, Mailpit and the mock Slack receiver. The earlier tests only used fake channels. It checks four flows:

  - a non-matching event creates no deliveries
  - a failing Slack delivery ends up dead, and an admin retry then sends it
  - a disabled channel stores the delivery as skipped
- [smoke.spec.ts](apps/web-e2e/src/smoke.spec.ts) is one Playwright test in the browser. A user adds a Slack target and a market alert, an injected event reaches the Slack mock, and the admin sees the delivery as Sent.

- **Outcome:** I rejected one GPT finding about where Playwright points its tests, with the reason in V-022.
